Question 15:
Listen to two people discussing the Volunteer in a clean-up program. Read the opinions below and decide whose opinion matches the statements, the man, the woman, or both the man and the woman. You can listen to the discussion twice.

(Man start)

Man: I watched a news report about the clean-up program yesterday. To be honest, I think the media made it sound much more successful than it really was.

Woman: I agree. They only showed the best parts and ignored many problems. The benefits of the program were clearly exaggerated.

Man: Exactly. And even with programs like this, I still think littering will always be a problem. Some people just do not care enough about public places.

Woman: Maybe, but I don't think we should give up. Volunteers can still make a difference.

Man: That's true, but the problem will never completely disappear.

Woman: For me, the reason why volunteers join is not very important as long as the trash is picked up. Some people say that those who join only want to look good on social media. Whether they do it because they care about the environment or because they want experience, the result can still be the same if they work hard.

Man: I beg to differ. If they don't care genuinely, they will stop doing it soon. In my opinion, instead of relying on fake volunteers, the authorities must implement strict

punishments like heavy fines. That is the only truly effective way to stop people from littering

Woman: I'm not sure it is the best way. Fines might help, but education is also important.

Man: Education helps, but without fines or punishment, many people will not change their behavior.


​ - Media exaggerates the benefits of the programme

​ - Littering will always be a problem

​ - The volunteers’ motivations do not affect the programme outcome

​ - Punishment is the most effective way to prevent littering

Question 15:
Listen to two people discussing the CHILDREN AND TEENAGERS/THE YOUNG WITH TECHNOLOGY Read the opinions below and decide whose opinion matches the statements, the man, the woman, or both the man and the woman. You can listen to the discussion twice.

(Man start)

Man: I've been thinking about how children and young people use technology nowadays. They seem very interested in learning through computers, tablets, and educational apps.

Woman: I agree. Technology-based lessons can make learning more enjoyable, and many children are excited to use digital tools in class.

Man: However, I think technology can also affect their communication skills. Some children spend so much time online that they find it difficult to communicate with people face to face.

Woman: Yes, I've noticed that too. They may feel confident when sending messages, but they sometimes struggle to have conversations without using a device.

Man: Another problem is that many families don't know how to manage their children's use of technology. I think parents need more support and guidance to set appropriate rules at home.

Woman: That may be true, but I also believe children can learn to control their own online behaviour. With proper education, they can understand when to stop using technology and how to interact responsibly online.


​ - Children are interested in technology-based learning

​ - Children have trouble communicating offline

- Families need help managing technology.

​ - Children can learn to regulate their online interactions

Question 15:
Listen to two people discussing the HOMESCHOOLING Read the opinions below and decide whose opinion matches the statements, the man, the woman, or both the man and the woman. You can listen to the discussion twice.

(Woman start)

Woman: I have been reading an article about homeschooling lately and comparing it with traditional schooling. What do you think?

Man: I've always thought one of the biggest advantages of homeschooling is the freedom it gives families. Children don't have to follow a fixed timetable, and lessons can be adapted to suit their interests and pace of learning.

Woman: I can see why people like that aspect, but I think there are other issues we need to consider. Not every parent is trained to teach. Some subjects can be quite challenging, and parents may not always have the knowledge or teaching skills needed to explain them properly.

Man: That's a fair point. Still, many parents put a lot of effort into preparing lessons and finding suitable learning materials.

Woman: Of course, but effort and expertise aren't always the same thing. Teaching requires specific skills that not everyone develops naturally.

Man: Another criticism I often hear is that homeschooled children miss out on social experiences because they aren't in a traditional classroom.

Woman: Actually, I'm not convinced that's true. Many homeschooled students join sports clubs, music groups, and community activities. Some of them probably interact with a wider range of people than children who spend most of their day with the same classmates.

Man: I suppose social opportunities can exist outside school if families actively look for them.

Woman: Exactly. The quality of social interaction matters more than where it happens.

Man: One thing that's definitely changed homeschooling over the years is technology. Online platforms make it much easier to access lessons and educational resources.

Woman: Absolutely. Students can now attend virtual classes, watch instructional videos, and even collaborate with other learners online. Those tools have made homeschooling far more effective than it used to be.

Man: I agree. Without modern technology, it would be much harder for families to provide such a wide range of learning opportunities.

Woman: That's true. Digital resources have transformed the whole experience.



​ - Homeschooling is more flexible

- Parents dont have enough experience to teach their children

- Homeschooling doesnt reduce social interaction.

​ - Technology helps homeschooling become more effective
